clue.text: Part of Israel destined for the firstborn

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A portion of the Holy Land is set aside as the inheritance of a first son.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym by description: the child born before all its siblings is the senior one of the family.

clue.text: Going through sheets, accountant calms down

indicators.note: something going through another passes into its interior, so the accountant sits inside the sheets

parts.note: plates are thin flat sheets of metal or glass
CA is the abbreviation for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper relaxes while working through the spreadsheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to soothe or pacify someone angry is to make them quieter.

clue.text: Intimate duo ultimately can't find convertible

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A close couple are frustrated in their hunt for a soft-top car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' reads as an adjective describing the duo, but it is a noun here. 'ultimately' takes O from duo, and 'convertible' rearranges O with CANTFIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: an intimate is a close friend trusted with one's secrets.

clue.text: Golden award framed by retro artist

indicators.note: a frame surrounds its picture, so the artist's letters go round the award
retro means looking backwards, so the artist's letters are turned round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A gilded prize sits in a picture frame made by an old-fashioned painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns the artist's two letters round and 'framed by' sets the award between them; the award is a British state honour, the artist a Royal Academy member.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour synonym: the fossil resin's yellow-orange hue is routinely described as golden.

clue.text: Animal died too soon in poem

indicators.note: arriving too soon means coming earlier than expected, so the letter for died moves forward to the front

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A creature meets an untimely end in a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too soon' moves the D of ODE from the middle to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female deer is one kind of beast.

clue.text: Issue taken on by sponsors

parts.note: issue here means offspring, and sponsors are those who make promises for a child at a baptism

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: sponsors at a christening accept spiritual responsibility for other people's offspring.

clue.text: Ape Biblical tribe's sound

indicators.note: sound says the tribe's name is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Simeon was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Mimic the noise made by an Old Testament people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' reads as a verb meaning imitate, but it is the animal. 'sound' says SIMEON is to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: the word covers any monkey or anthropoid primate.

clue.text: Polish prime minister pronounced play area fit for toddlers

parts.note: to sand a surface is to polish it smooth

indicators.note: pronounced says the prime minister's name is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: William Pitt was a British prime minister, both the Elder and the Younger

explanation.surface: Poland's leader declares a playground suitable for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb meaning to smooth. 'pronounced' gives PIT from PITT, the name of two 18th-century British prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a shallow box of grains where small children dig and build.

clue.text: Short chip breaking solid fuel of regular shape

indicators.note: what breaks something splits it open, so the shortened chip goes inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel

indicators.note: short says the word for chip loses its final letter

parts.note: a nick is a small chip or notch

explanation.surface: A stubby french fry snaps a neatly formed briquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chip' suggests fried potato or silicon, but it is a small notch; 'Short' drops its last letter and 'breaking' sets what is left inside the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: shaped like a cone, one of the regular geometric solids.

clue.text: Escort anticipated girl's rejection

parts.note: something due is expected or anticipated

indicators.note: rejection suggests sending back, so the girl's name is written backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A date saw the young woman's refusal coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection' turns ANN into NNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an older Spanish woman acting as chaperone accompanies a young lady.

clue.text: Muscleman buried by old criminal

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran gangster disposes of a heavy in a shallow grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges BURIED BY OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who develops a heavily muscled physique through weight training.

clue.text: Workers collectively vote for DJ

parts.note: TU is a trade union, workers organised collectively
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The staff jointly choose who plays the records.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey but is the British abbreviation for dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: American equivalent: the short form of tuxedo is what Britons call a dinner jacket.

clue.text: Frenchman's a hack, missing none of the action

parts.note: un is the French word for a
to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A French journalist of the tabloid kind sees everything that happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a film shown in full has had no scenes removed.

clue.text: Allows clubs in to record urban development

indicators.note: in places allows and clubs inside the word for record

parts.note: to tape is to record
to own something is to admit or allow it to be true
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: The council lets nightspots in so as to log the city's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allows' is the sense of admitting something is true, not permitting; 'in' sets that word and the card suit inside the recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: the built-up scenery of a city, the visible result of urban building.

clue.text: Case of delegate: did job and earned?

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: someone who served did a job

explanation.surface: A representative did the work and merited the reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what one has merited by one's efforts.

clue.text: The way something like plane cuts through stone

indicators.note: what cuts through something passes into the middle of it

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
a plane is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A carpenter's tool slices cleanly through rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not the tool or aircraft. 'cuts through' puts TREE inside ST, the abbreviation for the British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a road in a town is a way.

clue.text: Study headed by key university in former capital?

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece at the head comes first, so key and university go above study

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
to do a subject at school is to study it

explanation.surface: Research led by a leading college in a city that once governed a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is money, not a city: this was Portugal's currency before the euro. 'headed by' says the key and university sit on top of the word for study.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning description: capital in the sense of money, and this Portuguese currency is no longer in use.

clue.text: Plant from an outlet academic's written about

indicators.note: written about says the academic's letters go round the others

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written
a deli is a retail outlet selling fine foods

explanation.surface: A factory is the subject of a professor's paper on a retail store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory beside 'outlet', but it is the botanical kind; 'written about' wraps the academic round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common yellow-flowered weed is one member of the vegetable kingdom.

clue.text: Musical genre affecting outcome of election?

definitions.meaning: the big-band jazz style of the 1930s and 1940s
the shift of votes from one party to another, which decides who wins

explanation.surface: A style of music changes how the vote turns out.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a jazz dance-band style, and the movement of voters between parties that decides a result.

clue.text: Disappointed colleagues prepare to unload truck, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the idiom for failing one's team-mates, in the past tense as well as the present
a literal picture: lowering the hinged panel of a lorry before taking the load off

explanation.surface: Glum workmates get ready to empty a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for failing one's team, and a literal reading of lowering a lorry's flank panel.

clue.text: Nell standing up for king in custody dispute

indicators.note: one thing standing for another replaces it, so Nell's letters take the king's place

parts.note: to have charge of someone is to have custody of them
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: in a down entry standing up means reading from the bottom to the top

explanation.surface: Nell Gwyn defends Charles II in a row over who keeps the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns NELL into LLEN, and 'for' has it replace the R (rex) in CHARGE. Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to call a claim into question is to contest it.

clue.text: With temperature risen fully, stop drum

indicators.note: in a down entry a letter that has risen fully has gone all the way to the top

parts.note: to abort a mission is to stop it

explanation.surface: Once the heat has climbed all the way, quit beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risen fully' moves the T of ABORT from the bottom to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small medieval percussion instrument played with one hand alongside a pipe.

clue.text: Dreadful eyestrain dispensing with a sense of calm

indicators.note: dreadful means in a bad state, so the letters are disordered
to dispense with something is to do without it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: Awful tired eyes drive out any feeling of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensing with' drops the A from EYESTRAIN and 'Dreadful' rearranges EYESTRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a state of peaceful tranquillity.

clue.text: Lucid narrative in translation a very good thing

indicators.note: translation turns a text into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clear story rendered into another language is a real asset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges LUCID NARRATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: prudence, justice, temperance and fortitude are the four chief moral excellences.

clue.text: In island, mounting corruption gets one brooding

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

indicators.note: in a down entry mounting means climbing, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Growing sleaze on a small isle leaves someone sullen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brooding' is hatching eggs, not sulking. 'mounting' turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a heated apparatus that hatches eggs does the job of a sitting hen.

clue.text: Bore shut up about European levy

indicators.note: about says the word for shut up goes round the letter for European

parts.note: pent means confined or shut up
a rate is a local property tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tedious person finally went quiet on the subject of a Brussels tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is the verb meaning to drill, not a tedious person. 'about' puts E inside PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to drill into something is to pierce it.

clue.text: Finish off jump fast in Arctic conditions?

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them, to finish them off
to bound is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: A skier completes a leap at speed in polar weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means stuck firmly, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a ship held firm by frozen sea is stuck fast in polar weather.

clue.text: Bar selection's run out

indicators.note: out says the letter for run is taken away from the selection

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage selected from a longer work
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The pub's range of drinks has been used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is the preposition meaning other than. 'out' removes R from EXCERPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposition synonym: both mean apart from, as in all bar one.

clue.text: Weeds from moor spread minimally

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

indicators.note: minimally asks for the least possible amount of the word, its first letter only

explanation.surface: Unwanted plants from the heath have hardly travelled at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' is the verb for tying up a boat, not heathland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these broad-leaved plants are common garden nuisances.

clue.text: Fresh start, note, with firm

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
jelly or concrete that has set is firm

explanation.surface: A new beginning, jotted down, with a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: returning something to its initial state so it can begin again.
